newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Golden Valley shares dive after deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golden Valley shares dive after deal.

text.p: Shares in Golden Valley Mines NL dived 48 percent to an intraday low of six cents on heavy volume on Tuesday after reports of a deal on the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia that failed to mention Golden Valley's joint venture partner, PT Krueng Gasui.

Canadian-based Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday it had teamed up with U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoran Copper and Gold Inc to develop the deposit, estimated to contain more than 70 million ounces of gold that could be mined at a cost of US$96 an ounce.
The Indonesian government is yet to issue a statement.
PT Krueng Gasui (KG), associated with Joseph Merukh, owns an undisputed 10 percent stake in the Muara Atan Contract of Work, which contains part of the Busang deposit.
Merukh claims another 10 percent interest through PT Sungai Atan Perdana and an option for a further 20 percent of Busang.
KG filed a C$2 billion lawsuit on January 15 in Canada against Bre-X to reinforce its claim to the deposit.
Golden Valley's exposure to the deposit is through a technical assistance and financial deal with Merukh's companies.

Noting the continuing uncertainty of the deal, with the Indonesian government yet to issue its statement, and the horse trading seen so far, brokers said the game may not yet be over, although nervous investors had preferred to cut their positions.
"It might still be far from over," said a Melbourne dealer.
"Obviously, some investors are saying they just don't want to be there," he added, although he noted that both Golden Valley shares and options had bounced well off their early lows.

By 11.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), Golden Valley shares were three cents lower at 8.5 cents, off their six cent lows, on turnover of 18.5 million shares, while the options were at 1.4 cents lower at 2.8 cents, off early lows of 0.008, on turnover of 20.86 million options.
